Lecture 11: Binary choice and maximum likelihood

Economics 527: Econometric Methods

Author

Vadim Marmer, UBC

Binary choice

Binary choice model

  • Data: observations (Y_i, X_i), i = 1, \ldots, n.

  • Binary Y_i indicates the choice: Y_i \in \{0, 1\}

  • Examples:

    • in the labour force or not
    • went for a postgraduate degree or not
    • firm entered market i or not

  • Random (latent) utility from choice 1: V_i = X_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i

  • Observed and unobserved: \begin{aligned} V_i &: \ \text{unobserved} \\ X_i &: \ \text{observed characteristics} \\ \varepsilon_i &: \ \text{unobserved} \end{aligned}

  • Choice 1 when the utility is positive: \begin{aligned} Y_i &= \mathbf{1}(V_i > 0) \\ &= \mathbf{1}(X_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i > 0) \end{aligned}

  • Y_i generated from a nonlinear model.

Response probability

  • Assume: F, the CDF of \varepsilon_i given X_i, known: F(t) = \mathrm{P}(\varepsilon_i \le t \mid X_i = x) \quad \text{for all } x, t

  • Substitute the model: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) &= \mathrm{P}(x^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i > 0 \mid X_i = x) \\ &= \mathrm{P}(\varepsilon_i > -x^\top \beta \mid X_i = x) \\ &= 1 - F(-x^\top \beta) \\ \Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) &= 1 - F(-X_i^\top \beta) \end{aligned}

  • Assume: F symmetric around zero: 1 - F(-t) = F(t)

  • Response probability with a symmetric F: \boxed{\ \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = F(X_i^\top \beta)\ }

Linear probability model

Uniform errors

  • Suppose: \begin{aligned} & \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim \text{Uniform}(0, 1) \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & F(t) = t, \quad t \in (0, 1) \end{aligned}

  • Uniform CDF at -X_i^\top \beta: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) &= 1 - F(-X_i^\top \beta) \\ &= 1 + X_i^\top \beta \\ &= \underbrace{(\beta_1 + 1)}_{\text{intercept}} + X_{i,2}^\top \beta_2 \end{aligned}

  • Assume: 0 < -X_i^\top \beta < 1

  • X_i includes an intercept: X_i = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ X_{i,2} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta = \begin{pmatrix} \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \end{pmatrix}

  • Constant 1: absorbed by the intercept.

  • Definition. Linear probability model (LPM): \boxed{\ \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = X_i^\top \beta\ }

Connection of LPM to regression

  • Conditional mean of binary Y_i: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i\right] &= 1 \cdot \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) + 0 \cdot \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i) \\ &= \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) \end{aligned}

  • LPM \Longrightarrow linear regression of Y_i on X_i: \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i\right] = \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = X_i^\top \beta

Probit and logit

Probit

  • \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(0, 1), CDF \Phi: \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = \boxed{\ \Phi(X_i^\top \beta)\ } \qquad (\Phi \ \text{symmetric around zero})

Logit

  • \varepsilon_i \mid X_i logistic, CDF \Lambda: \begin{aligned} \Lambda(t) &= \frac{e^t}{1 + e^t} \\ &= \frac{1}{e^{-t} + 1} \\ &= \frac{1}{1 + \frac{1}{e^t}} \end{aligned}

  • Probability of each choice: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) &= \frac{e^{X_i^\top \beta}}{1 + e^{X_i^\top \beta}} \\ \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i) &= 1 - \frac{e^{X_i^\top \beta}}{1 + e^{X_i^\top \beta}} \\ &= \frac{1}{1 + e^{X_i^\top \beta}} \end{aligned}

  • Odds ratio: \frac{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i)}{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i)} = e^{X_i^\top \beta}

  • Log odds ratio: \boxed{\ \log \frac{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i)}{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i)} = X_i^\top \beta\ }

Identification

Scale of \beta and \varepsilon_i

  • Suppose \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2).

  • Rescaled coefficients and errors: \beta^* = \frac{\beta}{\sigma}, \qquad \varepsilon_i^* = \frac{\varepsilon_i}{\sigma}, \qquad \varepsilon_i^* \mid X_i \sim N(0, 1)

  • Divide by \sigma > 0 inside the indicator: \begin{aligned} Y_i &= \mathbf{1}(X_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i > 0) \\ &= \mathbf{1}\Big(X_i^\top \frac{\beta}{\sigma} + \frac{\varepsilon_i}{\sigma} > 0\Big) \\ &= \mathbf{1}(X_i^\top \beta^* + \varepsilon_i^* > 0) \end{aligned}

  • Example with scalar X_{i,2}, same distribution of Y_i given X_i: \begin{aligned} \text{1)} \quad & Y_i = \mathbf{1}(1 + X_{i,2} + \varepsilon_i > 0), \qquad \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(0, 4) \\ \text{2)} \quad & Y_i = \mathbf{1}\big(\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2} X_{i,2} + \varepsilon_i > 0\big), \qquad \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(0, 1) \end{aligned}

  • Only \beta / \sigma can be identified.

Location of \varepsilon_i and the intercept

  • Suppose \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2): \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) &= \mathrm{P}(X_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i > 0 \mid X_i) \\ &= \mathrm{P}(\varepsilon_i > -X_i^\top \beta \mid X_i) \\ &= \mathrm{P}\Big(\frac{\varepsilon_i - \mu}{\sigma} > \frac{-X_i^\top \beta - \mu}{\sigma} \ \Big|\ X_i\Big) \\ &= \Phi\Big(\frac{X_i^\top \beta + \mu}{\sigma}\Big) \qquad \Big(\frac{\varepsilon_i - \mu}{\sigma} \ \Big|\ X_i \sim N(0, 1)\Big) \end{aligned}

  • Intercept, X_i = (1, X_{i,2}^\top)^\top, \beta = (\beta_1, \beta_2^\top)^\top: \frac{X_i^\top \beta + \mu}{\sigma} = \underbrace{\frac{\beta_1 + \mu}{\sigma}}_{\text{intercept}} + X_{i,2}^\top \frac{\beta_2}{\sigma}

  • \mu: absorbed by the intercept.

Identification of probit

  • \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x): can be estimated from the data.

  • Invert \Phi: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) = \Phi(x^\top \beta) \\ \Longleftrightarrow\quad & \Phi^{-1}\big(\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)\big) = x^\top \beta, \qquad \beta \in \mathbb{R}^k \end{aligned}

  • Quantile of N(0, 1), with \Phi^{-1}(\tau) = z_\tau: z(x) = \Phi^{-1}\big(\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)\big) = z_{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)}

  • Pick values x_1, \ldots, x_k of X_i: k \times 1, linearly independent: \begin{aligned} \underbrace{\begin{pmatrix} z(x_1) \\ \vdots \\ z(x_k) \end{pmatrix}}_{k \times 1} &= \underbrace{\begin{pmatrix} \overset{1 \times k}{x_1^\top} \\ \vdots \\ x_k^\top \end{pmatrix}}_{k \times k} \beta \\ \Longrightarrow\quad \beta &= \begin{pmatrix} x_1^\top \\ \vdots \\ x_k^\top \end{pmatrix}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} z(x_1) \\ \vdots \\ z(x_k) \end{pmatrix} \end{aligned}

  • \beta: identified.

Identification of logit

  • Log odds ratio at X_i = x, identified from the data: r(x) = \log \frac{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)}{\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i = x)} = x^\top \beta

  • Same steps, r(x) in place of z(x): \beta = \begin{pmatrix} x_1^\top \\ \vdots \\ x_k^\top \end{pmatrix}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} r(x_1) \\ \vdots \\ r(x_k) \end{pmatrix}

Example: Walmart and town population

  • \text{Walmart}_i = 1: a Walmart in town i.

  • Logit given the population of town i: \mathrm{P}(\text{Walmart}_i = 1 \mid \text{Population}_i = x) = \frac{e^{\beta_1 + \beta_2 x}}{1 + e^{\beta_1 + \beta_2 x}}

  • Log odds ratio, identified from the data: r(x) = \log \frac{\mathrm{P}(\text{Walmart}_i = 1 \mid \text{Population}_i = x)}{\mathrm{P}(\text{Walmart}_i = 0 \mid \text{Population}_i = x)} = \beta_1 + \beta_2 x

  • Two town populations, x = 10{,}000 and x = 25{,}000: \begin{aligned} & r(10{,}000) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 \cdot 10{,}000 \\ & r(25{,}000) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 \cdot 25{,}000 \\ \Longleftrightarrow\quad & \begin{bmatrix} r(10{,}000) \\ r(25{,}000) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 10{,}000 \\ 1 & 25{,}000 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \end{bmatrix} \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \begin{bmatrix} \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 10{,}000 \\ 1 & 25{,}000 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} r(10{,}000) \\ r(25{,}000) \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}

Marginal effects

Marginal effects in the linear model, probit and logit

  • LPM: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i = x\right] = \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) = x^\top \beta \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \beta_j = \frac{\partial\, \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)}{\partial x_j} \end{aligned}

  • \beta_j: the same at every x.

  • Probit and logit, f: PDF of F: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) = F(x^\top \beta) \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \frac{\partial\, \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)}{\partial x_j} = f(x^\top \beta)\, \beta_j \end{aligned}

  • f(x^\top \beta)\, \beta_j: changes with x.

Average marginal effect (AME)

  • Definition. Marginal effect averaged over X_i: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{AME}_j &= \mathrm{E}\left[f(X_i^\top \beta)\, \beta_j\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[f(X_i^\top \beta)\right]\, \beta_j \end{aligned}

Maximum likelihood estimator (MLE)

Bernoulli trials

  • Consider a version with only Y_i: no varying regressors X_i.

  • Data Y_1, \ldots, Y_n \in \{0, 1\}, iid: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1) &= \theta_0 \in (0, 1) \\ \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0) &= 1 - \theta_0 \end{aligned}

  • \theta_0: true value of \theta.

  • PMF, y \in \{0, 1\}: \mathrm{P}(Y_i = y) = \theta_0^{\,y} (1 - \theta_0)^{1 - y}

  • A possible sample, one of 2^n: y_1, \ldots, y_n, \qquad y_i \in \{0, 1\}

  • Probability of the observed sample: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{P}(Y_1 = y_1, \ldots, Y_n = y_n) &= \prod_{i=1}^n \mathrm{P}(Y_i = y_i) \qquad \text{(independence)} \\ &= \prod_{i=1}^n \theta_0^{\,y_i} (1 - \theta_0)^{1 - y_i} \\ &= \theta_0^{\sum_i y_i} (1 - \theta_0)^{n - \sum_i y_i} \end{aligned}

Likelihood function and the MLE

  • Observed sample probability as a likelihood function of \theta: L_n(\theta) = \theta^{\sum_i Y_i} (1 - \theta)^{n - \sum_i Y_i}

  • Definition. MLE: \begin{aligned} \hat\theta &= \underset{\theta}{\arg\max}\ L_n(\theta) \\ &= \underset{\theta}{\arg\max}\ \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\theta) \end{aligned}

  • Average log likelihood, with \bar Y = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i: \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\theta) &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i \log \theta + \frac{1}{n} \Big(n - \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\Big) \log(1 - \theta) \\ &= \bar Y \log \theta + (1 - \bar Y) \log(1 - \theta) \end{aligned}

MLE in Bernoulli trials

  • First-order condition: \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \Big(\frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\theta)\Big) = \frac{\bar Y}{\theta} - \frac{1 - \bar Y}{1 - \theta}

  • \hat\theta solves: \begin{aligned} & \frac{\bar Y}{\hat\theta} - \frac{1 - \bar Y}{1 - \hat\theta} = 0 \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \boxed{\ \hat\theta = \bar Y\ } \end{aligned}

  • Weak LLN for \bar Y: \begin{aligned} \hat\theta = \bar Y &\to_p \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i\right] \\ &= 1 \cdot \theta_0 + 0 \cdot (1 - \theta_0) \\ &= \theta_0 \end{aligned}

Normal regression model

  • Normal regression with iid observations (Y_i, X_i): \begin{aligned} Y_i &= X_i^\top \beta_0 + U_i \\ U_i \mid X_i &\sim N(0, \sigma_0^2) \end{aligned}

  • PDF of U_i given X_i, at u: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_0^2}} \exp\Big(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma_0^2}\Big)

  • Distribution of Y_i given X_i = x: Y_i \mid X_i = x \sim N(x^\top \beta_0,\ \sigma_0^2)

  • PDF of Y_i at y given X_i = x, with u = y - x^\top \beta_0: \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_0^2}} \exp\Big(-\frac{(y - x^\top \beta_0)^2}{2\sigma_0^2}\Big)

MLE in the normal regression

  • Conditional likelihood: \begin{aligned} L_n(\beta, \sigma^2) &= \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp\Big(-\frac{(Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big) \\ &= \Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}\Big)^n \exp\Big(-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big) \end{aligned}

  • Average conditional log likelihood: \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\beta, \sigma^2) &= \log \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2 \\ &= \log\big((2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2}\big) - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2 \\ &= -\frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi\sigma^2) - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\, \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2 \end{aligned}

  • MLE of \beta: \begin{aligned} \hat\beta^{MLE} &= \underset{\beta}{\arg\max}\ \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\beta, \sigma^2) \\ &= \underset{\beta}{\arg\max}\ \Big(-\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2\Big) \\ &= \underset{\beta}{\arg\min}\ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - X_i^\top \beta)^2 \\ &= \hat\beta^{OLS} \end{aligned}

Conditional likelihood for probit and logit

  • iid observations (Y_i, X_i): \{(Y_i, X_i) : i = 1, \ldots, n\}

  • Probit and logit response probability: \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) = \underbrace{F(x^\top \beta_0)}_{=\, \theta_0(x)}

  • Conditional PMF, y \in \{0, 1\}: \mathrm{P}(Y_i = y \mid X_i) = F(X_i^\top \beta_0)^y \big(1 - F(X_i^\top \beta_0)\big)^{1 - y}

  • Probability of the observed outcomes given the regressors: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}(Y_1 = y_1, \ldots, Y_n = y_n \mid X_1, \ldots, X_n) \\ &= \prod_{i=1}^n \mathrm{P}(Y_i = y_i \mid X_i) \\ &= \prod_{i=1}^n F(X_i^\top \beta_0)^{y_i} \big(1 - F(X_i^\top \beta_0)\big)^{1 - y_i} \end{aligned}

Conditional log likelihood and grid search

  • Average conditional log likelihood: \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\beta) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \Big\{Y_i \log F(X_i^\top \beta) + (1 - Y_i) \log\big(1 - F(X_i^\top \beta)\big)\Big\}

  • MLE of \beta: \hat\beta^{MLE} = \underset{\beta \in \mathbb{R}^k}{\arg\max}\ \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\beta)

Consistency of the MLE

General setup

  • Data \{W_i : i = 1, \ldots, n\}, PDF or PMF f(w, \theta_0): W_i \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} f(w, \theta_0), \qquad \theta_0 \in \mathbb{R}^k: \ \text{true value}

  • Assume: common support \{w : f(w, \theta) > 0\} for all \theta.

  • Assume: \mathrm{E}\left[|\log f(W_i, \theta_0)|\right] < \infty.

  • Logit: W_i = (Y_i, X_i^\top)^\top and \theta = \beta.

  • f: conditional PMF of Y_i given X_i: f(w, \theta_0) = \Lambda(x^\top \theta_0)^y \big(1 - \Lambda(x^\top \theta_0)\big)^{1 - y}, \qquad w = (y, x^\top)^\top, \quad y \in \{0, 1\}

  • MLE, maximizer of the average log likelihood: \hat\theta = \underset{\theta}{\arg\max}\ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \log f(W_i, \theta)

  • To show (consistency): \hat\theta \to_p \theta_0

Consistency argument

  • \theta^*: unique maximizer of \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right].

  • Weak LLN for each \theta, then maximize both sides, under regularity conditions: \begin{array}{ccc} \dfrac{1}{n} \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n \log f(W_i, \theta) & \to_p & \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] \\[1ex] \Big\downarrow \ \arg\max & & \Big\downarrow \ \arg\max \\[1ex] \hat\theta & \to_p & \theta^* \end{array}

  • Consistency if the population maximizer is \theta_0: \boxed{\ \theta^* = \theta_0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \hat\theta \to_p \theta_0\ }

Jensen’s inequality and the population log likelihood

  • We will use Jensen’s inequality, h concave: \mathrm{E}\left[h(Z)\right] \le h\big(\mathrm{E}\left[Z\right]\big)

  • Claim. For all \theta: \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] \le \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right]

  • Proof, f(w, \theta_0): the true PDF of W_i: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] - \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta) - \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\log \frac{f(W_i, \theta)}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] \\ &\le \log \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{f(W_i, \theta)}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] \qquad \text{(Jensen's inequality, $\log$ concave)} \\ &= \log \int \frac{f(w, \theta)}{{\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}}\, {\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}\, dw \\ &= \log \underbrace{\int f(w, \theta)\, dw}_{=\, 1} \\ &= 0 \end{aligned}

Strict inequality and identification

  • Suppose \theta \ne \theta_0, \log strictly concave: \mathrm{E}\left[\log \frac{f(W_i, \theta)}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] < \log \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{f(W_i, \theta)}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right]

  • Unless the ratio is constant with probability one: \begin{aligned} & \frac{f(W_i, \theta)}{f(W_i, \theta_0)} = \text{const} \\ \Longleftrightarrow\quad & f(W_i, \theta) = \underbrace{\text{const}}_{=\, 1} \cdot f(W_i, \theta_0) \end{aligned}

  • Assume (identification), for all \theta \ne \theta_0: \mathrm{P}\big(f(W_i, \theta) \ne f(W_i, \theta_0)\big) > 0

  • Hence: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] < \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] \quad \text{for all } \theta \ne \theta_0 \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \theta^* = \theta_0 \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \hat\theta \to_p \theta_0 \end{aligned}

Identification in the logit

  • Logit: f(W_i, \theta) = \Lambda(X_i^\top \theta)^{Y_i} \big(1 - \Lambda(X_i^\top \theta)\big)^{1 - Y_i}

  • \Lambda strictly increasing: \Lambda(u_1) = \Lambda(u_2) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad u_1 = u_2

  • Suppose \theta_1 \ne \theta_0: \begin{aligned} f(W_i, \theta_1) = f(W_i, \theta_0) \quad &\Longleftrightarrow \quad X_i^\top \theta_1 = X_i^\top \theta_0 \\ &\Longleftrightarrow \quad X_i^\top \underbrace{(\theta_1 - \theta_0)}_{=\, a} = 0 \end{aligned}

  • To rule out X_i^\top a = 0 with probability one, assume: \mathrm{E}\left[X_i X_i^\top\right] p.d.: \begin{aligned} a \ne 0 \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad \mathrm{P}(X_i^\top a \ne 0) > 0 \\ &\Longrightarrow \quad \mathrm{P}\big(f(W_i, \theta_1) \ne f(W_i, \theta_0)\big) > 0 \end{aligned}

Asymptotic normality and standard errors

Gradient and Hessian

  • h : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}, gradient: \underset{k \times 1}{\frac{\partial h}{\partial \theta}} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial \theta_1} \\ \vdots \\ \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial \theta_k} \end{bmatrix}

  • Hessian: \underset{k \times k}{\frac{\partial^2 h}{\underset{k \times 1}{\partial \theta}\, \underset{1 \times k}{\partial \theta^\top}}} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial \theta_1 \partial \theta_1} & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial \theta_1 \partial \theta_k} \\ \vdots & & \vdots \\ \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial \theta_k \partial \theta_1} & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial \theta_k \partial \theta_k} \end{bmatrix}

  • Score of observation i, gradient of its log likelihood: \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta)

First-order condition and expansion

  • We will use the expansion of h around \theta_0: h(\hat\theta) \approx h(\theta_0) + \frac{\partial h(\theta_0)}{\partial \theta^\top} (\hat\theta - \theta_0)

  • First-order condition for \hat\theta, each element expanded around \theta_0: \begin{aligned} \underset{k \times 1}{0} &= \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \log f(W_i, \hat\theta)\Big] \\ &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \hat\theta) \\ &\approx \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \underbrace{\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}_{k \times 1} + \underbrace{\Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big]}_{k \times k} \underbrace{(\hat\theta - \theta_0)}_{k \times 1} \end{aligned}

  • OLS normal equations: \begin{aligned} 0 &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i \hat U_i \\ &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i (Y_i - X_i^\top \hat\beta^{OLS}) \\ &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i \big(U_i - X_i^\top (\hat\beta^{OLS} - \beta_0)\big) \end{aligned}

Solving for \sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0)

  • Solve for \hat\theta - \theta_0, then multiply by \sqrt{n}: \begin{aligned} & \Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big] (\hat\theta - \theta_0) \approx -\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0) \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \hat\theta - \theta_0 \approx -\Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big]^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0) \\ \Longrightarrow\quad & \sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) \\ &\qquad \approx -\Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big]^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0) \end{aligned}

  • Same form for the scaled OLS estimation error: \sqrt{n}(\hat\beta^{OLS} - \beta_0) = \Big(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i X_i^\top\Big)^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n X_i U_i

Average Hessian and scaled score

  • Weak LLN for the average Hessian, limit assumed negative definite: \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top} \to_p \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]

  • Variance of the score: \begin{aligned} \Omega_0 &= \mathrm{Var}\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right) \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\, \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^\top} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] \end{aligned}

  • Second-moment form of \Omega_0 and the CLT need: \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] = 0

  • CLT for the scaled score: \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0) \to_d N(0, \Omega_0)

Mean of the score

  • Assume: \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} and \int interchange.

  • Population first-order condition, \theta_0 = \arg\max_\theta \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right]: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] &= \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] \Big|_{\theta = \theta_0} \\ &= 0 \end{aligned}

  • A more direct argument: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] &= \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] \\ &= \int \frac{\partial f(w, \theta_0) / \partial \theta}{{\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}} \cdot {\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}\, dw \\ &= \int \frac{\partial f(w, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta}\, dw \\ &= \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \underbrace{\int f(w, \theta_0)\, dw}_{=\, 1} \\ &= 0 \end{aligned}

Sandwich form

  • Weak LLN for the average Hessian, CLT for the scaled score: \begin{aligned} \sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) &\approx -\Big[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big]^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0) \\ &\to_d -\Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} N(0, \Omega_0) \end{aligned}

  • Asymptotic variance, the Hessian symmetric: \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\theta) = \Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} \Omega_0 \Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1}

Information matrix equality

  • Claim. \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right] = -\Omega_0

  • We will use: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] &= \int \frac{\partial^2 f(w, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\, \frac{1}{{\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}} \cdot {\color{red} f(w, \theta_0)}\, dw \\ &= \frac{\partial^2}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top} \underbrace{\int f(w, \theta_0)\, dw}_{=\, 1} \\ &= 0 \end{aligned}

  • Differentiate the score: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^\top}\, \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^\top}\, \frac{\partial f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}{f(W_i, \theta_0)} - \underbrace{\frac{\partial f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}}_{\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}\, \underbrace{\frac{\partial f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta^\top}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}}_{\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^\top} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right] \\ &= \underbrace{\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 f(W_i, \theta_0) / \partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}{f(W_i, \theta_0)}\right]}_{=\, 0} - \Omega_0 \\ &= \boxed{\ -\Omega_0\ } \end{aligned}

Information matrix and asymptotic variance

  • Definition. Information matrix: I(\theta_0) = -\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]

  • I(\theta_0): symmetric, p.d.

  • Substitute \Omega_0 from the information matrix equality: \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AsyVar}(\hat\theta) \\ &= \Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} \underbrace{\Omega_0}_{=\, -\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]} \Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} \\ &= -\Big(\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} \\ &= \Big(-\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]\Big)^{-1} \\ &= I(\theta_0)^{-1} \end{aligned}

  • Asymptotic distribution of the MLE: \boxed{\ \sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) \to_d N\big(0,\ I(\theta_0)^{-1}\big)\ }

Standard errors

  • \hat\theta_j, \theta_{0,j}: element j of \hat\theta, \theta_0.

  • Estimator of \Omega_0: \hat\Omega = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial \log f(W_i, \hat\theta)}{\partial \theta}\, \frac{\partial \log f(W_i, \hat\theta)}{\partial \theta^\top}

  • Standard error of \hat\theta_j, from the average Hessian at \hat\theta: \text{std. err}(\hat\theta_j) = \sqrt{\frac{\Big(\Big[-\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \hat\theta)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\Big]^{-1}\Big)_{jj}}{n}}

  • Or from \hat\Omega: \text{std. err}(\hat\theta_j) = \sqrt{\frac{\big(\hat\Omega^{-1}\big)_{jj}}{n}}

  • t test of H_0: \theta_{0,j} = c vs H_1: \theta_{0,j} \ne c: |\hat\theta_j - c| / \text{std. err}(\hat\theta_j) > z_{1-\alpha/2} \Longrightarrow reject.

Estimated average marginal effect

AME estimator

  • AME estimator from \hat\beta and known f: \widehat{\mathrm{AME}}_j = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n f(X_i^\top \hat\beta)\, \hat\beta_j

Stein’s lemma and LPM slopes

Normal regressors and Stein’s lemma

  • \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i\right] = g(X_{i,2}): nonlinear, unknown.

  • AME, with g'(x) = \partial g(x) / \partial x: \mathrm{AME} = \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right]

  • Probit and logit: \begin{aligned} g(x) &= F(\beta_1 + x^\top \beta_2) \\ g'(x) &= f(\beta_1 + x^\top \beta_2)\, \beta_2 \end{aligned}

  • Stein’s lemma. \underset{1 \times 1}{X_{i,2}} \sim N(\mu_X, \sigma_X^2), g differentiable: \underbrace{\mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right]}_{=\, \mathrm{Cov}\left(g(X_{i,2}),\, X_{i,2}\right)} = \sigma_X^2\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right]

  • Proof: appendix.

  • Vector \underset{(k-1) \times 1}{X_{i,2}} \sim N(\mu_X, \underset{(k-1) \times (k-1)}{\Sigma}), \Sigma p.d.,
    g differentiable: \mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right] = \Sigma\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right]

LPM slope with a scalar normal regressor

  • Scalar X_{i,2} \sim N(\mu_X, \sigma_X^2), g differentiable.

  • LPM: population OLS of Y_i on 1 and X_{i,2}, slope \delta: \begin{aligned} \delta &= \frac{\overbrace{\mathrm{E}\left[(X_{i,2} - \mu_X) Y_i\right]}^{=\, \mathrm{Cov}\left(X_{i,2},\, Y_i\right)}}{\mathrm{E}\left[(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)^2\right]} \\ &= \frac{\mathrm{E}\left[(X_{i,2} - \mu_X) Y_i\right]}{\sigma_X^2} \\ &\overset{\text{LIE}}{=} \frac{\mathrm{E}\left[(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\, g(X_{i,2})\right]}{\sigma_X^2} \\ &= \frac{\sigma_X^2\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right]}{\sigma_X^2} \qquad \text{(Stein's lemma)} \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right] \\ &= \boxed{\ \mathrm{AME}\ } \end{aligned}

LPM slopes with vector normal regressors

  • Vector X_{i,2} \sim N(\mu_X, \Sigma), \Sigma p.d.

  • Population OLS slopes \delta (Y_i on 1, X_{i,2}): \begin{aligned} \delta &= \Sigma^{-1} \mathrm{Cov}\left(X_{i,2}, Y_i\right) \\ &= \Sigma^{-1} \mathrm{E}\left[(X_{i,2} - \mu_X) Y_i\right] \\ &\overset{\text{LIE}}{=} \Sigma^{-1} \mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right] \\ &= \Sigma^{-1} \Sigma\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right] \qquad \text{(Stein's lemma)} \\ &= \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right] \\ &= \boxed{\ \mathrm{AME}\ } \end{aligned}

  • Normal X_{i,2}: the LPM slopes equal the AME, for any differentiable g.

Summary

Binary choice and identification

  • Y_i = \mathbf{1}(X_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i > 0), \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim F \Longrightarrow \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = 1 - F(-X_i^\top \beta).

  • F symmetric around zero \Longrightarrow \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = F(X_i^\top \beta).

  • LPM: \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i\right] = \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) = X_i^\top \beta.

  • Probit: F = \Phi.

  • Logit: F(t) = \Lambda(t) = e^t / (1 + e^t).

  • Logit, log odds ratio: \log\big(\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i) / \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 0 \mid X_i)\big) = X_i^\top \beta.

  • \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2): only \beta / \sigma can be identified.

  • \varepsilon_i \mid X_i \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2): \mu absorbed by the intercept.

  • Probit: \Phi^{-1}\big(\mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x)\big) = x^\top \beta.

  • Probit and logit: k linearly independent values of X_i \Longrightarrow \beta identified.

Marginal effects

  • LPM: \partial\, \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) / \partial x_j = \beta_j at every x.

  • Probit and logit: \partial\, \mathrm{P}(Y_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) / \partial x_j = f(x^\top \beta)\, \beta_j.

  • \mathrm{AME}_j = \mathrm{E}\left[f(X_i^\top \beta)\right]\, \beta_j.

Maximum likelihood and consistency

  • W_i \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} f(w, \theta_0): \hat\theta = \arg\max_\theta \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \log f(W_i, \theta).

  • Assume: common support \{w : f(w, \theta) > 0\} for all \theta.

  • Assume: \mathrm{E}\left[|\log f(W_i, \theta_0)|\right] < \infty.

  • Bernoulli trials: \hat\theta = \bar Y.

  • Normal regression: \hat\beta^{MLE} = \hat\beta^{OLS}.

  • Probit and logit: \frac{1}{n} \log L_n(\beta) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{Y_i \log F(X_i^\top \beta) + (1 - Y_i) \log\big(1 - F(X_i^\top \beta)\big)\big\}

    • \hat\beta^{MLE} by numerical maximization, for example grid search.

  • Jensen’s inequality: \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta)\right] \le \mathrm{E}\left[\log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] for all \theta.

  • Under regularity conditions: \mathrm{P}\big(f(W_i, \theta) \ne f(W_i, \theta_0)\big) > 0 for all \theta \ne \theta_0 \Longrightarrow \hat\theta \to_p \theta_0.

  • Logit: \mathrm{E}\left[X_i X_i^\top\right] p.d. \Longrightarrow identification condition.

Asymptotic normality

  • Assume: \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} and \int interchange.

  • \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right] = 0.

  • \Omega_0 = \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\, \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^\top} \log f(W_i, \theta_0)\right].

  • Information matrix equality: \mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right] = -\Omega_0.

  • I(\theta_0) = -\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\partial^2 \log f(W_i, \theta_0)}{\partial \theta\, \partial \theta^\top}\right]: information matrix, p.d.

  • \sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) \to_d N\big(0,\ I(\theta_0)^{-1}\big).

  • \text{std. err}(\hat\theta_j) = \sqrt{(\hat\Omega^{-1})_{jj} / n}.

  • Or minus the average Hessian at \hat\theta in place of \hat\Omega.

AME estimator and Stein’s lemma

  • \widehat{\mathrm{AME}}_j = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n f(X_i^\top \hat\beta)\, \hat\beta_j.

  • Stein’s lemma, X_{i,2} \sim N(\mu_X, \sigma_X^2), g differentiable: \mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right] = \sigma_X^2\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right].

  • \mathrm{E}\left[Y_i \mid X_i\right] = g(X_{i,2}), X_{i,2} \sim N(\mu_X, \Sigma), \Sigma p.d. \Longrightarrow LPM slopes {\delta = \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right] = \mathrm{AME}}, for any differentiable g.

Appendix

Proof of Stein’s lemma

  • Suppose \underset{1 \times 1}{X_{i,2}} \sim N(\mu_X, \sigma_X^2), g differentiable.

  • PDF of X_{i,2}: f_X(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_X^2}}\, e^{-\frac{(x - \mu_X)^2}{2\sigma_X^2}}

  • Write the expectation with the normal PDF: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right] &= \int g(x)\, (x - \mu_X)\, f_X(x)\, dx \\ &= \sigma_X^2 \int g(x)\, \frac{x - \mu_X}{\sigma_X^2}\, f_X(x)\, dx \\ &= \sigma_X^2 \int g(x)\, \frac{x - \mu_X}{\sigma_X^2}\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_X^2}}\, e^{-\frac{(x - \mu_X)^2}{2\sigma_X^2}}\, dx \\ &= -\sigma_X^2 \int g(x)\, \Big(-\frac{x - \mu_X}{\sigma_X^2}\Big) \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_X^2}}\, e^{-\frac{(x - \mu_X)^2}{2\sigma_X^2}}\, dx \end{aligned}

  • Differential of f_X: \begin{aligned} d f_X(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_X^2}}\, e^{-\frac{(x - \mu_X)^2}{2\sigma_X^2}} \times \frac{-2(x - \mu_X)}{2\sigma_X^2}\, dx \\ &= -\frac{x - \mu_X}{\sigma_X^2}\, f_X(x)\, dx \end{aligned}

  • Integration by parts: \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g\, dh = g\, h \Big|_{-\infty}^{\infty} - \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} h\, dg

  • Continue, integrate by parts with h = f_X: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{E}\left[g(X_{i,2})(X_{i,2} - \mu_X)\right] &= -\sigma_X^2 \int g(x)\, d f_X(x) \\ &= \underbrace{\sigma_X^2 \lim_{a \to \infty} \Big[-g(x)\, f_X(x)\Big]_{-a}^{a}}_{=\, 0} \\ &\qquad + \sigma_X^2 \int f_X(x)\, dg(x) \\ &= \sigma_X^2 \int f_X(x)\, g'(x)\, dx \\ &= \boxed{\ \sigma_X^2\, \mathrm{E}\left[g'(X_{i,2})\right]\ } \end{aligned}
